SUMO simulation of traffic knowledge and reachable motion
Road restrictions and nearby vehicles change while the ego vehicle moves. Delayed observations can misrepresent available space.
A student laptop can reproduce traffic events and compare planning decisions using measured simulation data.
The referenced KARS work connects traffic knowledge with reachable-set planning. This implementation uses project-level approximations.
We study delayed and lost traffic knowledge. The full paper was unavailable, so we do not assert an unverified gap in its experiments.
Received packets become RDF constraints. The planner prunes motion, selects a chain and requests speed/lane changes.
SUMO, TraCI, simulated IoT, RDF/SPARQL, RS, corridor DP, SLSQP and control form a repeating loop.
A seeded channel delays or drops packets. Each snapshot retains its generation timestamp. No hardware sensor is claimed.
Static schema describes roads and lanes. Dynamic triples describe observed vehicles and active restrictions. SPARQL drives pruning.
Offline samples define actions. Online propagation uses x_next=x+v dt+0.5a dt² and v_next=v+a dt. The grid is finite.
Swept segments are checked against spatial, spatial-speed, spatial-temporal and spatial-temporal-speed restrictions.
Terminal lane endpoints define ancestor corridors. DP minimizes speed deficit, acceleration, lane switching and center distance.
SLSQP smooths longitudinal acceleration within bounds. Invalid optimization falls back to the feasible DP chain.
Vehicle occupancy grows with packet age. Missing or stale knowledge triggers controlled braking. Compare safety and progress together.
Construction, temporary lane blockage, lead braking, changed speed cap and traffic signal exercise the full pipeline.
Use the completed run CSV and JSON. Arrival, collision events, rule violations and clearance describe executed behavior.
A* searches the same feasible time-state graph. Basic RS omits traffic-rule pruning. All planners retain identical SUMO safety.
Explicit queries and rejection sources make decisions auditable. Tests and seeded scenarios support reproduction.
Add validated lateral dynamics and physical obstacles. Obtain the full paper for equation alignment. Calibrate uncertainty before real deployment.
The project demonstrates knowledge-driven local planning and an implementable delay-aware extension. Measured comparisons determine its benefit.
